page.layout: One page of text, main column centre-left; a narrow column of printed marginal notes at the far right edge of the scan, on the facing page (partly cut off). The digitiser's footer is excluded.

main_text.p: berit, ne inanitæ venæ humores excrementitios attrahant. At in magnis morbis, inprimis ijs qui oriuntur à sanguinis fluxu, ut pleuritis, statim quavis diei & noctis hora, neglecta præparatione, sanguis est demendus. In mora enim est magnum periculum; est enim magna necessitas, & vires constant. In principio itaque febrium ardentium sectio est instituenda. Idem fit in revulsione, partibus nimirum inflammatis.
Derivatio revulsionem sequitur. at si sanguinem parti impactum discutere, aut putrefacere nolis sed elicere, decurrendum erit ad minora præsidia; hirudines nimirum, cucurbitulas, scarificationem.

Hirudines bonæ (nec enim omnes conveniunt) aqua purissima, eaque sæpius mutata, eousque lavandæ sunt, donec omnem virulentiam & malignitatem deponant; tum partibus admotæ, (quibus trifidum vulnus infligunt) relinquendæ, dum sanguine turgidæ, sponte cadant. Multum sanguinis

page.notes: Marginal notes on the facing (right) page are cut off and only fragmentary (e.g. "Instr.", "sanguinis prolix", "melancholici", "pellum", "revulsio", "ad extrem"); they are too incomplete to transcribe reliably. Some words in the main text, such as "Hirudines" and "sanguine", are set in a slightly lighter impression and were read with care. The first line of the page is partly obscured at the spine.
